final_candidates.decision_summary: K51 lies immediately adjacent to the RKKRRQRRR TAR-binding motif; arginine strengthens arginine-phosphate RNA contacts. Conservative, charge-preserving, and directly aligned with enhancing transactivation.
Conservative lysine-to-arginine substitution near the core/basic region boundary that maintains positive charge while favoring stronger RNA/phosphate interactions. Plausible but unvalidated gain.
Arginine at position 54 enriches the basic domain, generally enhancing TAR binding and transactivation. Mechanistically plausible with moderate uncertainty.

stop_reason.detail: No evidence tools are available in S0-iter and further self-review is unlikely to change the Top-3 or its ranking.

history.rationale: Arginine substitution within the core cysteine-adjacent region preserves positive charge while enhancing RNA/protein interaction stability seen in clade variants; Lys-to-Arg is conservative and generally well tolerated.
Conservative substitution in the core/basic region preserves charge while being a common tolerated residue; mechanistically plausible but unvalidated.
Introducing positive charge just before the arginine-rich motif may strengthen TAR RNA binding affinity and transactivation; Gln-to-Arg is tolerated in variable loop regions.
Within the basic domain where arginine enrichment generally enhances TAR binding and transactivation.
Conservative Lys-to-Arg change near the ARM can increase electrostatic TAR RNA contacts and is common in natural Tat variants with robust transactivation.
K51 sits immediately adjacent to the RKKRRQRRR TAR-binding arginine motif; arginine strengthens RNA contacts, aligning directly with transactivation.
Highly conservative acidic substitution at the flexible N-terminus unlikely to disrupt function while slightly increasing stability.
Conservative N-terminal change with marginal expected effect on transactivation.
Adding positive charge between core and basic domains could enhance RNA binding; moderate risk of structural perturbation.
Positive charge near the basic domain could modestly help, but may perturb local structure.
Tyr at this position occurs in some natural variants and may improve P-TEFb-associated contacts; moderate uncertainty.
Y at H33 might enhance P-TEFb/CDK9 interaction analogously to H33Y-type gain-of-function variants, but evidence is weak; lowered confidence.
Conservative swap within the basic domain; minor effect expected but preserves ARM composition.
R53 is within the core arginine motif; lysine substitution typically weakens TAR arginine-phosphate contacts, so likely deleterious.

rejection.reason: R53 is within the core arginine motif; lysine substitution typically weakens TAR arginine-phosphate contacts, so likely deleterious.

history.rationale: Removing a proline in the N-terminal flexible region may increase chain flexibility for partner binding; risk of altering local conformation.
No mechanistic link to transactivation; proline loss may destabilize the N-terminal fold without benefit.

rejection.reason: No mechanistic link to transactivation; proline loss may destabilize the N-terminal fold without benefit.
